name: Shivam Autotech Limited
notes: Event 22-Jul-2025. FY24 annual report dated 12-Aug-2024 (financial statements approved 27-May-2024) precedes the event by 344 days and carries FY24 and FY23 - a clean pre-event window. CAUTION: the FY25 report RESTATES the FY24 Not Due / under-1-year split (Not Due 0.04 lakh restated to 639.06 lakh) and restates FY24 interest accrued and remaining unpaid (78.99 lakh restated to 72.99 lakh). Rows carry the figures as published in each report; the FY2024 row uses the FY24 report, i.e. what was knowable before the event. See findings.md. || SIGNAL RELIABILITY WARNING (added after within-company panel built): Shivam's Not Due-to-overdue migration REVERSES depending on which report is used for FY24. FY24 report: Not Due Rs 0.04 lakh, i.e. 100.0% of MSME dues overdue, giving +22.1 pp. FY25 report's FY24 comparative: Not Due Rs 639.06 lakh, i.e. 57.9% overdue, giving MINUS 20.0 pp. The company's own Not Due share across years is 34.2% (FY22), 24.4% (FY23), then either 1.1% or 46.7% (FY24), then 47.3% (FY25). The FY25-report version fits that series smoothly; the FY24-report version is a wild outlier. ASSESSMENT: the FY24 report figure is more likely a reporting error than a real collapse in Not Due, which would make Shivam's migration signal SPURIOUS. Shivam's other indicators are unaffected: MSMED interest accrued rose 0.73 -> 0.79 -> 1.33 across FY23-FY25, and non-MSME payables fell 32% in FY24. Treat Shivam as NOT evidence for the migration signal until the FY24 discrepancy is resolved with the company's filings. VERIFICATION ATTEMPTED: the BSE-hosted FY24 annual report (filed 31-08-2024, Fld_ReSubmit=0, i.e. never revised) was compared against the separately-sourced copy and the ageing table is IDENTICAL (Not Due 0.04). The FY24 report contains only one payables ageing table, so there is no internal cross-check. The discrepancy is therefore genuine and cannot be resolved from public filings alone; it needs the company's confirmation. Shivam remains excluded from the event evidence. || RESOLUTION ATTEMPT 2 - CORRIGENDUM FOUND: Shivam filed a Corrigendum to the FY2023-24 Annual Report with BSE on 16-09-2024 (announcement 'Corrigendum for unforeseen printing errors in the company's Annual Report for FY 2023-24', attachment 778d9d39-b58b-4d7b-a6cb-5c2a2a1b2eb7.pdf, 3 pages, scanned). It lists corrections for annual report pages 94, 95, 105, 108, 110, 112, 114, 115, 116, 121 and 135 - including errors as small as 0.01 lakh and a misspelling of 'Gurugram'. PAGE 117, WHICH CARRIES THE TRADE PAYABLES AGEING TABLE, IS NOT CORRECTED. The company therefore reviewed the FY24 report to one-paisa precision and did NOT treat the Not Due figure of 0.04 lakh as an error. This SHIFTS the balance of evidence toward the as-filed FY24 figure being intentional, and the FY25 comparative being a regrouping (the FY25 report carries only a generic 'previous year figures have been regrouped/restated' note). STATUS: upgraded from disputed to a QUALIFIED event observation. Report the headline both ways - conservatively n=1 event (Setco only), or n=2 including Shivam. Still unexplained by the company.

name: Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar Limited
notes: Event = CARE downgrade to CARE D from CARE B+; Negative on 29-Mar-2025 on expected default of a Rs 268 crore OCD instalment. FY24 annual report filed with BSE 31-05-2024, 302 days before the event. FY23 figures were cross-checked against the FY23 report's own columns and are IDENTICAL - no restatement. INDUSTRY-CRITICAL CAVEAT: in sugar, dues to sugarcane farmers do NOT sit in trade payables. Rs 2,361 crore of this company's Rs 2,494 crore 'Other payables' (Note 27, other current liabilities) is cane price dues routed through a statutory cane-price escrow account under the UP Sugar Cane Act 1953. The Schedule III trade payables ageing therefore measures the WRONG liability for this industry. Any sugar company added to this dataset must have its cane arrears captured separately. No Not Due column. MSME book immaterial (0.05% of trade payables). graph_valid FALSE - suppliers are farmers, customers are traders/OMCs; no named counterparty. || TIER: Anchor/end-producer: buys sugarcane from farmers, sells sugar/alcohol/power to traders and OMCs.

name: Nectar Lifesciences Limited
notes: Event = CARE downgrade to CARE BB-/A4 (Rating Watch Negative) from CARE BB/A4+ on 16-Jul-2025. FY24 annual report filed with BSE 14-08-2024, 336 days before the event. Reported in Rs MILLIONS; converted by dividing by 10. No Not Due column; ageing runs from due date. THRESHOLD EDGE CASE: msme_book_material is FALSE at 2.59% of trade payables, yet MSME payables ROSE 583% in the pre-event year - the clearest signal in the company. This shows the 5% materiality threshold must gate LEVEL comparisons only, never growth signals. See DATA_DICTIONARY section 5 trap 3. MSMED note is narrative, not tabular: only principal unpaid and interest under s.16 are disclosed, so the other MSMED fields are empty (not nil). REVISED AFTER CONTROLS: signal_path was msme_balance_growth, but control BGL_C (a company CARE UPGRADED) posted MSME growth of +629% against Nectar's +583%. MSME balance growth therefore does NOT discriminate and has been retired as a signal. Nectar still fires on payables/revenue, which rose 20.9% to 24.9% while both controls FELL ~2 points.

name: Bharat Gears Limited
product_category: gears for tractors and commercial vehicles
abandoned_reason: No qualifying distress event in FY22 or later: CARE reaffirmed CARE BBB; Stable on 03-Oct-2023 and subsequently UPGRADED the bank facilities (Sep-2024 revised PR). Operating cycle worsened 29d to 41d in FY23 but no downgrade, negative outlook, default or going-concern qualification.
notes: CONTROL, matched to SHIVAM (both gear manufacturers, tier-1, similar size). Non-distress confirmed: CARE reaffirmed CARE BBB; Stable on 03-Oct-2023 and UPGRADED the bank facilities in Sep-2024. Best disclosure in the dataset - has BOTH a Not Due and an Unbilled column. Reported in Rs LAKHS. IMPORTANT CONTROL RESULT: MSE payables rose 7.3x (Rs 1.46 cr to Rs 10.64 cr) and the MSE overdue share rose 20.8% to 36.1% in FY24, in a company that was UPGRADED. This is a false-positive on the msme_balance_growth signal and a partial false-positive on the not_due_migration signal. Total trade payables FELL 8% over the same period. See findings.md. MAJOR FINDING: Bharat Gears is the ONLY company in the dataset that discloses 'The amount of principal paid beyond the appointed day' - the brief's original PRIMARY SIGNAL - as its own line with non-zero values: Rs 9.21 cr in FY23 falling to Rs 3.20 cr in FY24, a 65% improvement, exactly what a healthy company should show. It also discloses 'Principal amount remaining unpaid beyond 45 days' (Rs 0.08 cr FY23, Rs 0.78 cr FY24). The contrast inside one company is the point: the STOCK figures (MSME balance, overdue share) rose sharply and look like distress, while the FLOW figure fell sharply and correctly says healthy. DISCREPANCY: MSMED Note 32.2 principal unpaid (Rs 1,091.96 / 149.97 lakh) differs slightly from Note 23 trade payables MSE (Rs 1,064.21 / 146.31 lakh); both recorded as printed.
role_history: Checked 2026-09-08 as a DISTRESS candidate and disqualified - the Oct-2023 CARE action is a reaffirmation at CARE BBB; Stable and the facilities were UPGRADED in Sep-2024. Promoted to the CONTROL cohort on the same evidence. Previously carried as two rows (company_id BGL and BGL_C) with the same NSE symbol BHARATGEAR; merged to a single identity 'BGL' on 2026-09-08 per brief section 4.5. The abandoned-distress row's abandoned_reason is preserved below.

name: Balrampur Chini Mills Limited
notes: CONTROL, matched to BHS (both large UP-based sugar millers). Non-distress: profitable and growing throughout the window - PBT rose from Rs 396.97 cr (FY23) to Rs 610.19 cr (FY24) - with no rating downgrade, no default and no going-concern qualification. Reported in Rs LAKHS. MSME payables 100% Not Due in BOTH years; every MSMED payment-delay line nil. THE STRONGEST SINGLE DISCRIMINATOR IN THE DATASET: trade payables are 5.0% of revenue (FY24) against Bajaj Hindusthan's 59.0%, on comparable revenue scale (Rs 5,594 cr vs Rs 6,077 cr). This REFINES the sugar caveat: a healthy sugar mill carries almost no trade payables because it pays cane dues promptly, whereas the distressed one carries Rs 3,541 cr in its under-1-year bucket AND a further Rs 2,361 cr of cane dues in an escrow account under other payables. Cane arrears show up in BOTH places for a stressed miller. || TIER: Anchor/end-producer: buys sugarcane from farmers, sells sugar/ethanol/power.
